text: If something consistently makes your life worse, it doesn't belong in your life. Hey guys, today I want to continue talking about men's main rules, principles that you should follow if you want to live a good life as a man. And once again, today's rule is, if something consistently makes your life worse, it doesn't belong in your life. What do I mean by that? Let me give you a simple analogy. Imagine you're walking in your favorite shoes. They are comfortable, proven, you love them. And suddenly, a small stone gets inside. It hurts, it's annoying. Every step is uncomfortable. What do you do? You stop, you take the stone out, you throw it away. Right? You don't say, well, the stone is already there, maybe I should adapt. You don't say, maybe it will get better tomorrow. You don't say, I'll suffer now, but one day walking will feel amazing again. No, you remove it immediately. But for some reason, when it comes to relationships, friendships, and people, men lose this basic logic. You start dating a woman, and suddenly your life gets worse. You're stressed, you can't sleep, you constantly feel guilty, you lose focus at work, your confidence drops, your mood is trashed. You start drinking more, escaping more, numbing yourself. And instead of asking, why is this happening? You say, relationships are supposed to be hard. Love is work. I just need to try harder. Maybe I can fix her. Maybe it will get better later. No, that's the stone in the shoe talking. A relationship that constantly makes you feel miserable is not normal. A partner who brings chaos, guilt, anxiety, and negativity into your life is not challenging you to grow. And this applies not only to women, but also to friends, business partners, anyone. If after meeting someone you regularly think, why did I even go there? That's your answer. Life is hard enough already. You don't need to voluntarily add people who make it harder. The rule is simple. If someone consistently takes your peace, your energy, your focus, your joy, they don't belong in your life. Cut them off the same way you remove a stone from your shoe. And one last thing. Rules only work if you actually follow them. Writing them down means nothing. Quoting them means nothing. But living by them changes your life for the better. So choose people who add to your life, not take away from it.
